memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot him." - Gen 40:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all Joseph had done for him, the chapter ends on a painful note: "The chief cupbearer... did not remember Joseph; he forgot him." Joseph had asked only one thing — "remember me" — and the cupbearer, restored to comfort and position, promptly forgot the man who had brought him hope in prison. Joseph would remain in that dungeon two more long years (Gen 41:1), waiting, forgotten by the very person he had helped.

How deeply this can wound: to help someone, to be a blessing to them, and then to be forgotten the moment they no longer need us. Many of us know the sting of being overlooked, unappreciated, or left behind by those we have served. It is one of the quiet heartaches of life.

But here is the truth that runs deeper than the disappointment: though people forget, God never does. The cupbearer forgot Joseph, but God did not. In fact, God was using this very delay — two more years in prison — to bring Joseph to the palace at exactly the right moment. What felt like being forgotten was really God's perfect timing at work.

There is a beautiful contrast here. Joseph said "remember me" to a man who forgot him. Later, a dying criminal would say to Jesus, "Remember me when you come into your kingdom" — and Jesus never forgot him (Luke 23:42-43). People may forget us, but our God remembers His own. If you feel forgotten today, take heart: you are held in the memory of a God who never forgets.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I known the sting of being forgotten by those I helped?
2. Do I trust that God remembers me even when people don't?
3. Can I trust God's timing when I feel left waiting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when people forget me, remind me that You never do. Thank You that even my seasons of waiting are held in Your perfect timing. Help me to trust the God who always remembers His own. Amen.
